newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha falls to 5-month lows.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha falls to 5-month lows.

text.p: The naphtha market fell to a six-month low in Japan and a five-month low in Singapore due to softer crude and weak demand in Asia, traders said on Monday.

In Singapore, naphtha April swaps shed 70 cents per barrel from Friday to $21.50/$21.70 while Japan's open-spec first-half June dropped $5.00 per tonne to $208.00/$209.50, the lowest since early October.

Physical trade in Singapore was thin but traders assessed premiums notionally at a maximum of $1.00 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, putting wet barrels at $22.50/$22.70, lifting late April-early May, the lowest since early November.
Traders in North Asia said the drop was due to a combination of arbitrage cargoes heading in from the West, naphtha cracker turnarounds in South Korea in May and weaker crude.

South Korean oil refiner Yukong Ltd has had additional naphtha exports since it extended the shutdown of its 8,000-bpd reformer No.1 until the end of June due to weak gasoline demand, an industry source said. The shutdown was reviewed late in March.
But the refiner was not pushed to offer any naphtha on the market because it had sufficient storage.
The secondary refining unit, which processes naphtha into reformate for either gasoline blending or further production into petrochemical BTX, was originally closed on January 24 due to poor margins.
"It (the shutdown extension) is not so much bad margins but weak demand for gasoline," a source said.

Despite the shutdown of production, Yukong has become an aggressive seller to Taiwan and just late last week was awarded Taiwan's tender for 95-octane unleaded reformate for first-half May delivery, with the second cargo awarded to Dutch trader Vitol, and a leaded cargo to Swiss trader Glencore, traders
said.

The bearish sentiment since the low Taiwan awards continued to bear down on the Singapore fob market with 95-octane offered aggressively by two sellers - a European major and a Singapore trader - at $26.35 and $26.50 per barrel for late April cargoes. The lowest offer on Friday was at $27.00.
The weaker gasoline market also saw a lower award into Pakistan's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources' tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of 80-octane leaded gasoline which closed March 31.

It bought the two 25,000-tonne cargoes at $25.43 per tonne over Mideast naphtha spot quotes, c-and-f, for delivery in the first and last weeks of May from U.K.-based trading company Hascombe, an official said.
"When we scrapped the tender in early March, the offer was $7.50 higher than this award," he said.

The ministry usually makes its import purchases through quarterly tenders across the barrel, but had issued a separate gasoline tender after receiving high offers in its original tender for second quarter requirements.

Pakistan received offers of around $30 per tonne over Mideast naphtha quotes c-and-f for the cancelled second quarter tender--nearly double the $16.745 premium it paid Hascombe for its first quarter purchases, sources said.
Pakistan doubled its May purchases to two cargoes due to the scheduled shutdown of a 63,000-bpd refinery for 20-days from April 25, the official said.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
